data.final_week_advice: Focus on timed practice and reviewing weak units 7 and 8.
data.summary: This 8-week plan prioritizes the student's weak units, Differential Equations and Applications of Integration, by introducing them early in weeks 2 and 3. The schedule balances foundational concepts in differentiation and integration with targeted review, ensuring all units are covered before the final two weeks are dedicated to mixed review and timed practice.

weeks.focus: Master limits and continuity to build a foundation for derivatives.
tasks: Do 15 multiple-choice questions on estimating limits from graphs and tables (1.3, 1.4).
Complete a worksheet on algebraic limit properties, focusing on factoring and rationalizing (1.5).
Review the definition of continuity and solve 5 problems determining if functions are continuous at specific points (1.2).

weeks.focus: Introduce differential equations early to address weakness in Unit 7.
tasks: Solve 10 problems modeling situations with differential equations, identifying variables and rates (7.1).
Verify 5 solutions for differential equations by substituting back into the original equation (7.2).
Sketch slope fields for 3 differential equations and identify equilibrium solutions (7.3).

weeks.focus: Reinforce differential equations through live instruction and practice.
tasks: Attend live class on Unit 7 topics 7.1 and 7.2.
Do 10 free-response questions on slope fields and reasoning about solutions (7.4).
Review class notes and solve 5 additional problems on verifying solutions (7.2).

weeks.focus: Cover differentiation fundamentals and chain rule.
tasks: Calculate derivatives for 10 functions using the power rule and product/quotient rules (2.5).
Apply the chain rule to differentiate 8 composite functions (3.1).
Estimate derivatives at a point using limit definition for 3 functions (2.3).

weeks.focus: Master implicit differentiation and inverse functions.
tasks: Differentiate 6 implicit equations and find slopes of tangent lines (3.2).
Differentiate 5 inverse functions and inverse trigonometric functions (3.3, 3.4).
Connect differentiability and continuity by analyzing 4 functions for smoothness (2.4).

weeks.focus: Apply differentiation to real-world contexts and motion.
tasks: Solve 5 related rates problems involving geometric shapes (4.4).
Analyze straight-line motion graphs to determine position, velocity, and acceleration (4.2).
Interpret the meaning of derivatives in 3 non-motion applied contexts (4.1, 4.3).

weeks.focus: Review analytical applications of differentiation and integration basics.
tasks: Use the Mean Value Theorem to prove 3 statements about functions (5.1).
Find global and local extrema for 4 functions using the First Derivative Test (5.2, 5.4).
Approximate areas using Riemann sums for 3 functions with different partition sizes (6.2, 6.3).

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed practice focusing on weak units.
tasks: Complete a 45-minute timed section of multiple-choice questions covering all units.
Do 3 free-response questions on Applications of Integration (8.1, 8.2, 8.4).
Review error log and redo 5 previously missed problems from Units 7 and 8.
